answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with randomized peer audits: a small, unpredictable sample of each agent's transactions is checked by independent peers, the way a river tests every stone it carries. A fake identity must keep its whole history consistent, not just one polished sonnet of a claim, because any audit can expose it — and exposure burns the shale-thin reputation it built. Each sybil therefore pays continuous upkeep to stay believable, so running a thousand fakes costs a thousand times the maintenance of one honest agent.
